about: The codes Care Management's rules name, by calendar year, with the minutes, days and rules CMS sets for each (see src/Domain/Schedule.php). A year's entry is "final" from the year's final rule, or "proposed" from its proposed rule, which the module doesn't use; "from" names the year it repeats except for "changes". CPT numbers only, with labels in our own words, never AMA's descriptions (Seth, 2026-10-24). HCPCS Level II codes are CMS's.
terms: CPT is a registered trademark of the American Medical Association. No CPT descriptor is reproduced here; the labels are ours (CC0). HCPCS Level II codes are published by CMS.

2026.source: The CY 2026 physician fee schedule final rule (FR 2025-19787, 90 FR 49266, 2025-11-05) and the earlier rules and CMS documents it leaves standing: MLN909188 (June 2025), MLN909432 (January 2026), the CCM, BHI and APCM FAQs, the CY 2017, 2020, 2024 and 2025 rules, and the Medicare Claims Processing Manual, chapter 12.

sources.rule: "CPT time rules apply." (MLN909432, January 2026, page 7) and "Note: CPT time rules apply to general BHI and CoCM services." (page 13); for G2214, "CPT time rules would apply, consistent with the guidance in the CPT codebook for CPT codes 99492-99494" (CY 2021 PFS final rule, 85 FR 84548). CMS names "the general CPT rule regarding the midpoint for certain timed services" (Medicare Claims Processing Manual, chapter 12, 30.6.1.B): a unit of time counts once more than half of it is done. The "from" values apply that rule to CMS's times; CMS's documents don't print them.
sources.99492: "70 minutes initial calendar month" (MLN909432, page 13, BHI Coding Summary): from 36, past the midpoint of 70.
sources.99493: "60 minutes per subsequent calendar month" (MLN909432, page 13): from 31, past the midpoint of 60.
sources.99494: "Each additional 30 minutes per calendar month" (MLN909432, page 13), used "as an add-on code with base CPT codes 99492 and 99493" (page 8): each unit from 16 minutes past the base code's full time, so the first at 86 minutes in a first month and 76 in a later one.
sources.G2214: "30 minutes of behavioral health care manager time per calendar month" (MLN909432, page 13; page 8: "covers the first 30 minutes in a month", for when "you don't meet the number of minutes needed to bill using the current coding"): from 16, when 99492's 36 or 99493's 31 isn't met.

2027.source: The CY 2027 physician fee schedule proposed rule (FR 2026-14327, 91 FR 43842, 2026-07-16; comments closed 2026-09-14). Not final: the module never uses a proposed year (src/Domain/Schedule.php). This entry is checked against the final rule when it is published, and released with what it finalized.
notes: RPM and RTM: "practitioners reporting RPM or RTM services must furnish a separately reportable initiating visit in association with the onset of RPM or RTM services", "initiated by the billing practitioner during a face-to-face (in-person or telehealth) visit" (91 FR 43892). A look-back of 0 years: every RPM or RTM enrollment needs its own initiating visit recorded.

RTM: "we are proposing to require that RTM services also be furnished only to established patients" (91 FR 43892). An initiating visit at the onset makes the patient established, so the look-back of 0 covers it.

RPM and RTM: "We are proposing to only allow payment for RPM or RTM services when furnished by clinical staff employed by the practice" (91 FR 43893). The record can't tell who employs a user, so nothing would be counted differently; if finalized, the guide and README say it.

RPM and RTM treatment management: the proposed rule removes the clinical staff inputs from 99470, 99457, 99458, 98979, 98980 and 98981's values (91 FR 43894): a change to what they pay, not to the minutes or who may log them.

Considered, with comment invited, not proposed: four G-codes in place of the 17 remote monitoring codes, GRPM1 and GRTM1 for set-up and GRPM2 and GRTM2 per calendar month with 2 or more days of data and at least 20 minutes of treatment management (91 FR 43894-95), and the same for RHCs and FQHCs.

CCM, PCM, BHI, CoCM, APCM and its add-ons: new values only; no code, minute or rule change. G2211 becomes a modifier and GACP1/GACP2 are new advance care planning codes; neither is a service this module counts.
